## What the method does

epiForest screens a case-control SNP data set for interacting loci in two stages. A random forest
with every SNP as a three-level factor ranks the SNPs by gini importance; a sliding window
sequential forward feature selection (SWSFS) adds SNPs in that order and keeps the first set whose
out-of-bag error is the smallest in a window of 20. The kept candidates are then tested one, two
and three at a time with the B statistic of Zhang and Liu (2007), Bonferroni-corrected for all
the SNPs screened.

> Jiang R, Tang W, Wu X, Fu W. A random forest approach to the detection of epistatic interactions
> in case-control studies. *BMC Bioinformatics* 10(Suppl 1):S65 (2009).
> [doi:10.1186/1471-2105-10-S1-S65](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-10-S1-S65)

The authors' program is lost; this package rebuilds the method from the paper's text.

## Install

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("jeonglab-bcm/fossil/PMC2648748/package")
```

```{r load}
library(epiforest)
packageVersion("epiforest")
```

## Example input

The bundled example has 300 cases and 300 controls genotyped at 60 SNPs, simulated from the
paper's threshold model (model 3); `snp17` and `snp44` are the disease loci.

```{r input}
ex <- read_genotypes(example_path())
dim(ex$geno)
table(status = ex$status)
ex$geno[1:5, 1:8]
```

## Run epiForest

```{r run}
fit <- epiforest(ex$geno, ex$status, ntree = 500, window = 20, seed = 1)
fit$swsfs$k                          # candidates kept by SWSFS
colnames(ex$geno)[fit$candidates]
reported <- fit$tests[fit$tests$reported, c("order", "snps", "given", "B", "df", "p", "p_adj")]
reported$snps <- vapply(strsplit(reported$snps, ","),
                        function(z) paste(colnames(ex$geno)[as.integer(z)], collapse = ","), "")
reported
colnames(ex$geno)[fit$identified]
```

```{r plots}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
plot(fit$gini, pch = 19, cex = 0.6, xlab = "SNP", ylab = "Gini importance")
points(fit$order[1:2], fit$gini[fit$order[1:2]], col = "red", cex = 1.4)
plot(fit$swsfs$errors, type = "b", pch = 19, cex = 0.5, xlab = "Number of top SNPs",
     ylab = "Out-of-bag error")
abline(v = fit$swsfs$k, lty = 2)
par(op)
```

## Compare with the expected output

`example_expected.csv` was written by the script that generated the data, from its own NumPy and
SciPy code: which SNPs are the disease loci, their B statistics and chi-squared tests.

```{r compare}
expected <- read.csv(example_path("example_expected.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
expected
col_of <- function(s) match(strsplit(s, ";")[[1]], colnames(ex$geno))
ok <- c()
for (i in which(expected$test == "B")) {
  b <- b_test(ex$geno, ex$status, matrix(col_of(expected$snps[i]), nrow = 1))
  ok[paste("B", expected$snps[i])] <- isTRUE(all.equal(c(b$B, b$p),
    c(expected$statistic[i], expected$p[i]), tolerance = 1e-8))
}
cs <- chisq_single(ex$geno, ex$status)
for (i in which(expected$test == "chisq")) {
  j <- col_of(expected$snps[i])
  ok[paste("chisq", expected$snps[i])] <- isTRUE(all.equal(c(cs$statistic[j], cs$p[j]),
    c(expected$statistic[i], expected$p[i]), tolerance = 1e-8))
}
disease <- col_of(expected$snps[expected$test == "disease_snps"])
ok["disease SNPs identified"] <- all(disease %in% fit$identified)
ok
cat(sum(ok), "of", length(ok), "checks match the expected output\n")
stopifnot(all(ok))
```

## Your own data

`read_genotypes()` reads a CSV file with a `status` column (1 case, 0 control) and one column per
SNP holding 0, 1 or 2 copies of the minor allele, with no missing values (impute or drop them
first). `epiforest()` takes the genotype matrix and the status vector:

- `ntree`: trees per forest. The paper used one million trees for its genome-wide data and does
  not say how many for its simulations; 500 (randomForest's default) is fast, more trees give a
  smoother out-of-bag error curve and usually a larger candidate set.
- `window`: the SWSFS window (20 in the paper).
- `alpha`, `max_order`: the significance level and the highest interaction order tested.

The result holds `gini` (one value per SNP), `swsfs$errors` (the out-of-bag error of each forest
built), `candidates`, `tests` (every test with its B statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value,
Bonferroni-adjusted p-value and whether it is reported; `given` lists the SNPs a conditional test
conditions on) and `identified` (the SNPs in a reported test). The comparators of the paper,
`chisq_single()` and `stepwise_lr()`, and its simulation design, `simulate_dataset()`, are also in
the package.

## The paper's full study

The reproduction of the paper's simulation study (Figs 2 and 3) with this package, and what came
back, is in [`PMC2648748/`](https://github.com/jeonglab-bcm/fossil/tree/main/PMC2648748) of the
fossil repository; the results page is <https://jeonglab-bcm.github.io/fossil/PMC2648748/>.
